items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 31 at 12:52AM AKDT until October 31 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
Steady snowfall through Broad Pass has tapered off to scattered snow
showers.  Steady, heavy snowfall is not expected to continue.

items.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 31 at 12:52AM AKDT until October 31 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
Gusty east winds will continue to rapidly diminish as a frontal
boundary reaches the coast and begins to dissipate over the next
couple of hours.  Strong to damaging winds are not expected to
continue.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 31 at 12:52AM AKDT until October 31 at 2:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Visibility one half mile or less at times.
Total snow accumulations 10 to 15 inches.

* WHERE...Thompson Pass.

* WHEN...Until 2 AM AKDT early this morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady snow will taper off to snow showers
through Thompson Pass overnight tonight.  Additional light snow
accumulations are likely through much of the day on Saturday, but
heavy snowfall rates will diminish by early Saturday morning.
items.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 30 at 11:44PM AKDT until October 31 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Light freezing rain and snow expected. Total snow
accumulations up to three inches with a glaze of ice.

* WHERE...Central Arctic Plains, and Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Travel may be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An initial band of freezing rain is expected
to impact areas around Deadhorse with a lull Friday night. Chances
return across a wider area including the Dalton Highway north of
the Brooks Range and the Arctic Coast from Nuiqsut eas
items.areas: Central Beaufort Sea Coast; Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast; Central Arctic Plains
items.instruction:
Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 30 at 10:00PM AKDT until October 31 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree

If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 30 at 4:04PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:

* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon. Heaviest snow expected from

could reduce visibility.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 30 at 2:29PM AKDT until October 31 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Northwest winds 30 to 45 mph with gusts up to 60 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Unalaska and Nikolski.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest wind gusts will begin this
evening and last through early Saturday morning, then diminish
through the rest of Saturday.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.
